name: Pale olive grey
lede: Pale olive grey is a light, dusty khaki, the library's lightened variant of [[olive-grey]], and our archive finds it in one painting in sixteen.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The nearest named color on file is [[corydalis-green]], 4.3 ΔE off [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas places it at plate LI, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same patch as yellowish gray, about 5.9 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. Measured in LCH it has lightness 80, chroma 13 and hue 111 degrees, close to [[beige]] and [[ecru]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 1,171 of 23,781 paintings, about 4.9 percent, as photographed, making it one of the more common named colors we track; the within-painting lens finds it in 846 [2]. That is ahead of 88 percent of our named colors [2]. It is most often a light tone, in 51 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 406 of 8,345 paintings, 4.9 percent of the 8,345 paintings (406 of them) we have from that century, about 1.4 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Eugène Boudin is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 33 archived works, 3.8 times the typical rate, and it is also over-represented in British paintings, 88 of 593, about 2.5 times what would be expected [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[light-celandine-green]] and [[leek-green]] [2].
